confidence_notes: I made six web searches: one for the RBA rate and five for food and drink prices. The food and drink results were search-result summaries of aggregator and crowd-sourced sites (Mylifeelsewhere, Citycost, Nomadranker, Wise, Expatistan), plus some hotel menu prices. They disagree with each other, and several have unclear update dates. Restaurant meal and coffee anchors are the firmest: cappuccino was about $4-5, an inexpensive meal about $5-9, and a mid-range dinner for two about $17-39. Alcohol is only served in licensed hotels and some restaurants, so beer, cocktail and wine anchors lean toward hotel-bar and licensed-restaurant prices. Those were roughly OMR 2-5 for beer, OMR 4-8 for cocktails and OMR 3-7 for a glass of wine. I converted at the fixed OMR peg of about 2.6 USD. The cocktail and wine anchors come from those listed ranges, not from a fixed ratio to beer. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge, with no accommodation searches. Muscat has few registered hostels, so the hostel anchors are the least certain. July is the hot low season, so hotel rates may run below the annual average.
comparable_city_reasoning: Oman is the cheapest GCC country by Numbeo-style indexes. Muscat restaurant prices are reported as noticeably lower than Dubai's, and Muscat's cost of living as roughly 15-26% below Abu Dhabi's and Dubai's. I positioned it as a mid-priced Gulf city, cheaper than Dubai or Abu Dhabi, with alcohol priced at licensed-venue levels.
